Majority of U.S. public school students are in poverty
Everyone with the means is taking their children out of public school leaving only children of parents that plain ol' don't care and the extremely impoverished. It's a terrible combination.

Growing up I went to Patriot street Kindergarten in Somerset PA. I think we were the last class. It was an old house, with four large rooms for classrooms. We had four teachers and no principal. Those four women did everything. They had a clothing closet if you had no coat, or boots, or mittens, or you wet yourself. They had mothers bring in a snack once a month for the whole class and every class had exactly 31 children. Everyone had to pay for their own milk, though I got reduced milk. I paid a quarter a day for my milk. Everyone else was 40 cents. I sensed the payment was more than for milk since I don't think it was a public school and reduced milk in the first grade was 10 cents.

On the first day of school they had a line where you got a dental check up, eye check up, chiropractic check up, your shots, clothes if you needed them, notebooks and crayons, and then you met your teacher. There were other things too, but it's been so long. When my mother found out that the school was not run by what she expected, she seemed shocked. I don't know how they ran it, but it was a safe haven.

We had plays, music, made maple syrup, visited the library, a pet goldfish, and story time. We had a lot of fun. We could count to 100, add simple problems, tell you the weather, season, day and month. Now school is more like a meat grinder. It isn't the safe haven it was for children...but it seems teachers are adopting these same strategies now that my Kindergarten had just to get by on a large scale. They need to in every school.

There are a lot of parents that just do not care. They don't try. They live their life and say the school needs to do everything else. I don't want my children around kids who, because of neglect and abuse, have major issues emotionally and otherwise. I know they will have to learn to deal with these sorts of people eventually, but childhood should be a safe haven. I try to expose them, a little at a time, to the suffering of other children without loving, caring parents without letting my children romanticize or idealize the traumatized child's delinquent behaviour. In short we homeschool and try to selectively allow people into their lives.

In the process we saved a family off the street and watched them gain footing. We have been friends ever since, with it being almost 4 years since they got on their own after our assistance. The parents obviously cared for their children in this family, but they didn't have enough knowledge to enrich their lives while being so far down. Now I am happy to report they have their daughter in band and the other graduated and employed. The father is employed full time and has been ever since. Some people just need to know you care, are there for them, and will hold their hand through it all.

Another family we tried to help, ended up with my child seeing a child living in a trailer with no floors or windows. The child in question had to catch food to eat. No medical care or education that we knew of at the time. He was placed with his mother and when she recieved him, she recieved nothing but a boy. Think about a child, where you must even give the clothes on his back to the people he was with before. She called out for help and I answered. I provided books, clothing, medicine, rides to doctors, groceries, dinner, tutoring, and even baby sitting services for her. In the end, her son threatened my daughter with violence and the mother lied constantly and asked for favors and money. She refused help getting work, counseling, a driver's license, parenting advice, or disability. She refused help to get her child health insurance, counseling, and away from some dangerous elements. We had to walk away from the situation, even though I know that child will not be able to give correct change by 18 unless the authorities step in and handle it. Yes, because of the threats of harm to my daughter I did go to the authorities.

Meanwhile my children have chores, part-time jobs, are home schooled daily and are with in range of their grade for their age. They have food, dinner every night, breakfast in the mornings even if it is something odd or pancakes (which isn't the healthiest thing). They have clean clothes, visit the doctor, and have physical therapy twice a week for those that need it. They go to karate classes and swimming in the summer. They go on vacations to grandmas and this year to Georgia. We aren't middle class, by far. We manage by cutting out everything else, to the bone. We do not get food stamps...but we grow food. We do not have cell phones at all...but we have a tablet I can use in hot spots for messages. We have one car. I stay home and manage the house, gardens, appointments, lessons, meals, chores, homeschooling, and animals. It's sad ...the only kids left in public school are the ones no one cares about or whose parents can't afford to take them out either in money or time.
